questions.prompt: Under the C++26 draft, what does this program print?
options: Nothing; it is ill-formed because the generator must take an `integral_constant` parameter
questions.explanation: The generator constructor calls the callable once for each lane index `i`, passing `integral_constant<simd-size-type, i>`, which converts implicitly to `int`. So the lanes are 0, 1, 4 and 9. `reduce` with its default `std::plus<>` adds all lanes, giving 14. The answer 6 is the sum of the indices, not of the squares.

questions.prompt: Under the C++26 draft, what happens with this function?
options: It returns true if every lane of `a` is less than the matching lane of `b`
It returns true if any lane of `a` is less than the matching lane of `b`
It is ill-formed: `a < b` is a `basic_mask`, which has no conversion to `bool`
It compiles, but which lanes are tested is implementation-defined
questions.explanation: Comparing two `vec` objects is an element-wise operation that returns `mask_type`, one boolean per lane. `basic_mask` deliberately has no `operator bool`, because "all lanes" and "any lane" are both plausible meanings. You state which one you want with `all_of(a < b)` or `any_of(a < b)`. For a per-lane choice instead of a branch, use `select`.

questions.prompt: Under the C++26 draft, what happens with this code?
options: Lane 0 becomes 5 and the other lanes stay 1
All four lanes become 5
It compiles, but the assignment changes a temporary and has no effect
It is ill-formed: `operator[]` returns `value_type` by value, which cannot be assigned to
questions.explanation: `basic_vec::operator[]` returns the element as a prvalue of `value_type`. Assigning to a prvalue of a scalar type is ill-formed, so the code does not compile, and the temporary answer is wrong for the same reason. This is intentional, because a lane inside a register is not an addressable object. To change some lanes, build a new vector with `select`, or use a generator.

questions.prompt: Under the C++26 draft, which line is ill-formed?
options: Line A only
Line B only
Line C only
Lines B and C
questions.explanation: The operands of `basic_vec`'s operators are vectors, so a scalar must be converted by the broadcast constructor. For an arithmetic argument, that constructor requires the conversion to be value-preserving, meaning every value of the source type is representable in the element type. `int` to `double` is value-preserving, but `int` to `float` is not, because `float` cannot represent every 32-bit `int`. So only line C is ill-formed. Writing `2.f` or `std::cw<2>` fixes it.

questions.prompt: Under the C++26 draft, what are the four lanes of `v`?
options: `{1, 2, 3, ?}`, where the last lane is indeterminate
Undefined behavior: four elements are read from a three-element array
questions.explanation: A partial load produces `mask[i] && i < size ? data[i] : T()` for each lane, with every lane enabled when no mask is given. Lane 3 is past the end of the range, so it is value-initialized to 0.0f and memory past the array is never read. That is the difference from `unchecked_load`, which requires at least `V::size()` elements and would have undefined behaviour here.

questions.prompt: Under the C++26 draft, which of these declarations is well-formed?
options: Only (1)
(1) and (3), but not (2)
All three
None: different element types never convert
questions.explanation: The converting constructor between `basic_vec` specializations of the same width is `explicit` exactly when the element conversion is not value-preserving or would lower the conversion rank. `float` to `double` is value-preserving, so (1) is an implicit conversion. `double` to `float` is not, so the constructor is explicit: copy-initialization (2) is ill-formed, while direct-initialization (3) is fine. Without (2) the function compiles.

questions.prompt: Under the C++26 draft, which of these is guaranteed to name an enabled `basic_vec` specialization on every conforming implementation?
options: `std::simd::vec<bool, 4>`
`std::simd::vec<long double, 2>`
`std::simd::vec<float, 128>`
`std::simd::vec<float, 64>`
questions.explanation: `deduce-abi-t<T, N>` names an ABI tag for every vectorizable `T` and every `N` from 1 up to an implementation-defined maximum that is not smaller than 64, so `vec<float, 64>` must work. Widths above 64 may or may not be supported. `bool` and `long double` are not vectorizable types at all, so those specializations are disabled everywhere.

questions.prompt: Under the C++26 draft, what does this program print?
options: Nothing; it is ill-formed because the masked `reduce` always needs an explicit identity element
questions.explanation: The masked `reduce` returns `identity_element` when `none_of(mask)` is true, and no lane exceeds 100 here. For `plus<>`, the default operation, the identity defaults to `T()`, which is 0. An explicit identity is required only for operations other than `plus<>`, `multiplies<>`, `bit_and<>`, `bit_or<>` and `bit_xor<>`. The answer 4 ignores the mask.
